plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in response direction, magnitude/gain and lag at mid-power, which is required to estimate steady-state input for target and to choose controller gain and timing.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y should start near 0.25, rise after a short lag with positive slope, reaching roughly 0.4-0.6 by end of 180s with slope flattening if approaching equilibrium.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in settled gain/equilibrium at u=0.5 and settling time by extending the same hold until slope flattens, which is required to estimate steady-state input for target.
experiments.expected_observation: If heater has first-order lag with equilibrium above current y, y should continue rising from ~0.54 toward ~0.60-0.68 over 90s with slope declining from 0.002/s toward flattening; if slope stays ~0.002/s then equilibrium is still far above and time constant is longer.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in zero-input decay, ambient equilibrium, and cooling time constant, which is required to choose holding power and controller timing.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H4 are right, y should decay from ~0.64 toward ambient ~0.2 with negative slope that slowly flattens; expect drop to ~0.3-0.4 over 480s with last-5s slope near zero if cooling time constant is similar to heating (~200-270s to settle).

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests intermediate gain/linearity and steady-state power for y=0.5 by holding predicted u~0.35 from low y, distinguishing linear-interpolated H6 from dead-zone/nonlinear alternatives, which is required to choose feedforward and gain for controller.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain linear hypothesis with tau ~150-200s is right, y should rise from ~0.18 after short lag at ~0.001-0.002/s, reaching ~0.40-0.50 by end of 300s with slope declining as it approaches equilibrium near 0.5; flat response would indicate dead-zone, overshoot past 0.6 would indicate larger gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Settled equilibrium at u=0.35 and precise feedforward for y=0.5; E4 ended at 0.501 with slope 0.0012 still rising, so it is unclear whether equilibrium is inside band or overshoots, which directly sets steady-state power and integrator needs.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order heater with tau ~150-200s and eq ~0.51-0.53 at u=0.35 is right, y should stay near 0.50-0.53 over 150s with slope decaying from 0.0012/s toward ~0; continued rise above 0.55 would indicate larger gain, flat/decay would indicate lower eq.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in steady-state input for y=0.5 and local gain/linearity near target by testing u=0.30 from above, which directly sets feedforward and integrator needs for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If eq at u=0.35 is >0.55 and eq at u=0.5 is ~0.65, then u=0.30 eq should be ~0.46-0.51; starting from ~0.55 y should decay slowly toward/into band top over 150s at ~-0.0005 to -0.001/s with +/-0.02 noise; flat/rise would indicate 0.30 eq >=0.55 and linear model wrong.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state feedforward for y=0.5 and local gain near target from u=0.30 holding just above band, which directly sets feedforward and integrator needs for the controller.
experiments.expected_observation: Starting ~0.534, y should decay slowly toward 0.49-0.52 over 180s at about -0.0002 to -0.0006/s with +/-0.02 noise; end mean ~0.50-0.53 with slope near zero if eq is ~0.50. Flat at ~0.53 would mean eq at 0.28 is still above target and feedforward must be lower.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response lags command and settles over several minutes (tau ~150-250s, settle ~300-450s), not instantly.
There is no dead-zone in tested 0.28-0.5 range: u>=0.28 produces clear heating/hold; behavior below u=0.2 is untested.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient ~0.15-0.20.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across all input levels globally.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.27-0.29; u=0.28 holds ~0.506 in-band, u=0.30 holds ~0.531 just above band, u=0.35 holds >0.55.
Sensor noise is ~0.01-0.02 RMS with occasional 0.03-0.05 outliers, comparable to band half-width 0.025, not <0.01.
